quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct answer.
quests.passage: [AI Writing Assistants in Schools] As AI writing tools become more common, some teachers have shifted their assignments to focus less on the final essay and more on the drafting process itself, requiring students to submit outlines, early drafts, and short reflections on their revisions. This approach makes it harder for students to simply submit AI-generated work as their own, while still allowing them to use such tools for brainstorming or feedback.
quests.question: Why have some teachers shifted focus to the drafting process?
options: It eliminates the need for grading essays
It makes it harder to submit AI-generated work as one's own
It allows students to skip writing entirely
It requires less time from teachers
quests.correctAnswer: It makes it harder to submit AI-generated work as one's own
quests.hint: The reason for the shift is explained in the second sentence.
quests.explanation: The passage says focusing on the drafting process makes it harder for students to pass off AI-generated work as their own.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct answer.
quests.passage: [Managing Chronic Pain] Rather than relying solely on medication, many chronic pain specialists now recommend a combined approach that includes gentle movement, sleep improvement, and stress reduction alongside any prescribed treatment. Patients who follow this broader approach often report better long-term results than those who depend on medication alone, though specialists stress that every patient's plan should be personalized.
quests.question: What do patients following the broader approach often report?
options: Faster short-term relief only
No noticeable improvement at all
A complete elimination of all pain
Better long-term results than those using medication alone
quests.correctAnswer: Better long-term results than those using medication alone
quests.hint: The reported outcome is compared to medication-only treatment.
quests.explanation: The passage says patients using the broader, combined approach often report better long-term results than medication alone.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct answer.
quests.passage: [Workplace Diversity Training] After a company's diversity training focused only on a single mandatory workshop each year, leadership noticed little measurable change in hiring or promotion patterns. When the company shifted to ongoing, smaller discussions integrated into regular team meetings, they began to see a more meaningful shift in workplace culture over the following two years.
quests.question: What change helped the company see a more meaningful shift in culture?
options: Adding a second yearly workshop
Hiring an outside consultant
Making the training completely optional
Shifting to ongoing discussions in regular team meetings
quests.correctAnswer: Shifting to ongoing discussions in regular team meetings
quests.hint: The successful change is described in the last sentence.
quests.explanation: The passage says shifting to ongoing discussions in team meetings led to a more meaningful cultural shift.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct answer.
quests.passage: [Cultural Immersion Homestays] Language schools increasingly encourage students to stay with local host families instead of hotels, arguing that daily immersion accelerates fluency far more than classroom instruction alone. Former students often describe the experience as initially uncomfortable, since navigating unfamiliar customs and routines requires constant adjustment, but ultimately more rewarding than any textbook could provide.
quests.question: How do former students often describe the homestay experience?
options: Initially uncomfortable but ultimately more rewarding
Consistently relaxing from the very start
Less effective than classroom study
Similar to staying in a hotel
quests.correctAnswer: Initially uncomfortable but ultimately more rewarding
quests.hint: The description covers both an early feeling and a later one.
quests.explanation: The passage says students describe the experience as initially uncomfortable but ultimately more rewarding.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct answer.
quests.passage: [Urban Heat Islands] Cities are often several degrees warmer than surrounding rural areas, a phenomenon known as the urban heat island effect, caused largely by dark pavement and buildings absorbing and re-radiating heat. Some cities have begun painting rooftops white or planting more trees along streets, both of which have been shown to noticeably lower local temperatures.
quests.question: What has been shown to noticeably lower local temperatures in cities?
options: Painting rooftops white and planting more street trees
Building taller skyscrapers downtown
Reducing the number of cars
Installing more streetlights
quests.correctAnswer: Painting rooftops white and planting more street trees
quests.hint: The effective solutions are named in the last sentence.
quests.explanation: The passage says painting rooftops white and planting more trees have been shown to lower temperatures.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct answer.
quests.passage: [Gap Year Experiences] Contrary to the assumption that a gap year delays academic progress, several long-term studies suggest that students who take a structured gap year before university often report higher motivation and slightly better grades once they begin their studies. Researchers believe the extra time allows students to clarify their goals before committing to a specific field.
quests.question: What do researchers believe explains the improved outcomes after a gap year?
options: Gap years make coursework easier overall
Students earn money to pay for tuition
The extra time allows students to clarify their goals
Universities lower requirements for gap year students
quests.correctAnswer: The extra time allows students to clarify their goals
quests.hint: The researchers' explanation is in the last sentence.
quests.explanation: The passage says researchers believe the extra time helps students clarify their goals before starting university.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct answer.
quests.passage: [Independent Game Developers] Unlike large studios with hundreds of employees, many independent game developers work alone or in small teams, often funding projects through crowdfunding platforms before a single line of code is written. While this approach carries significant financial risk, it also gives developers far more creative control over the final product than they would have working for a major publisher.
quests.question: What advantage do independent developers gain from this approach, according to the passage?
options: Guaranteed funding for every project
Access to large marketing budgets
Far more creative control over the final product
Protection from financial risk
quests.correctAnswer: Far more creative control over the final product
quests.hint: The advantage is described in the last sentence, contrasted with the risk mentioned before it.
quests.explanation: The passage says independent developers gain far more creative control, despite the financial risk involved.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct answer.
quests.passage: [Participatory Budgeting] Under participatory budgeting, residents of a district vote directly on how a portion of the local public budget should be spent, choosing between proposals such as new playgrounds, street repairs, or community centers. Supporters argue the process increases civic engagement, since residents who help decide how money is spent are more likely to stay involved in local issues afterward.
quests.question: Why do supporters say participatory budgeting increases civic engagement?
options: It reduces the total amount of taxes collected
Residents who help decide spending stay more involved afterward
It replaces the need for local elections
It guarantees every proposal gets funded
quests.correctAnswer: Residents who help decide spending stay more involved afterward
quests.hint: The supporters' reasoning is explained in the last sentence.
quests.explanation: The passage says supporters believe residents who participate in budgeting decisions stay more engaged in local issues.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct answer.
quests.passage: [Elder Care Planning] Financial planners increasingly advise adult children to discuss long-term care preferences with aging parents well before a health crisis forces a rushed decision. These early conversations, though sometimes uncomfortable, tend to result in choices that better reflect the parent's actual wishes rather than decisions made under sudden pressure.
quests.question: Why do planners recommend having these conversations early?
options: It reduces the cost of care significantly
Decisions better reflect the parent's wishes than rushed choices
It avoids the need for a legal will
It guarantees government financial support
quests.correctAnswer: Decisions better reflect the parent's wishes than rushed choices
quests.hint: The benefit of early conversations is explained in the last sentence.
quests.explanation: The passage says early conversations tend to result in choices that better reflect the parent's actual wishes.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct answer.
quests.passage: [Improving School Lunch Programs] After research linked poor nutrition to lower classroom concentration, one school district redesigned its lunch menu to include more whole grains, fresh vegetables, and less processed sugar. Cafeteria staff initially worried students would reject the healthier options, but participation in the lunch program actually increased once students adjusted to the new menu.
quests.question: What happened to lunch program participation after the menu changed?
options: It dropped sharply and never recovered
It stayed exactly the same
It was cancelled due to low interest
It actually increased once students adjusted
quests.correctAnswer: It actually increased once students adjusted
quests.hint: The outcome is stated in the last sentence, despite staff's initial worry.
quests.explanation: The passage says participation increased once students adjusted to the new, healthier menu.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct answer.
quests.passage: [Circadian Rhythms and Shift Work] Sleep scientists have long known that the body's internal clock, or circadian rhythm, struggles to adapt to rotating night shifts, which can lead to chronic fatigue and increased health risks over time. Some hospitals have begun scheduling nurses on fixed shifts instead of rotating ones, a change that early data suggests may reduce fatigue-related errors.
quests.question: What change have some hospitals made regarding nurse schedules?
options: Reducing the total number of night shifts
Requiring longer breaks between shifts
Switching from rotating shifts to fixed shifts
Eliminating night shifts completely
quests.correctAnswer: Switching from rotating shifts to fixed shifts
quests.hint: The specific scheduling change is described in the last sentence.
quests.explanation: The passage says some hospitals switched to fixed shifts instead of rotating ones to reduce fatigue-related errors.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct answer.
quests.passage: [Language Loss and Translation] Linguists estimate that a significant portion of the world's languages could disappear within this century, as younger generations in many communities shift toward more widely spoken languages for economic opportunity. Some communities are now recording elders speaking their native language, hoping the archives will preserve pronunciation and vocabulary even if daily use continues to decline.
quests.question: Why are some communities recording elders speaking their native language?
options: To create official government translation records
To teach the language exclusively in schools
To sell the recordings to researchers
To preserve pronunciation and vocabulary even if use declines
quests.correctAnswer: To preserve pronunciation and vocabulary even if use declines
quests.hint: The communities' goal is explained in the last sentence.
quests.explanation: The passage says communities hope the recordings will preserve pronunciation and vocabulary despite declining daily use.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct answer.
quests.passage: [A Shift Toward Modular Furniture] As more people move between rental apartments every few years, furniture companies have responded by designing modular pieces that can be reconfigured into different shapes rather than replaced entirely. A shelf, for instance, might be rearranged into a room divider or a desk, depending on a new apartment's layout.
quests.question: Why have furniture companies started designing modular pieces?
options: Modular furniture is required by new housing laws
People move between rental apartments frequently
Traditional furniture has become too expensive to produce
Renters prefer furniture with bright colors
quests.correctAnswer: People move between rental apartments frequently
quests.hint: The reason is given in the first sentence.
quests.explanation: The passage says the trend responds to people moving between rental apartments every few years.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct answer.
quests.passage: [A Rise in Community Tool Libraries] Similar to a public library for books, tool libraries allow members to borrow items like drills, ladders, and lawnmowers for a small fee or membership, rather than buying tools they might use only once or twice a year. Advocates say the model reduces both individual spending and the environmental cost of manufacturing rarely used equipment.
quests.question: What two benefits do advocates claim for tool libraries?
options: Faster tool repairs and free delivery
Higher tool quality and longer warranties
Reduced individual spending and reduced environmental cost
More storage space and lower rent
quests.correctAnswer: Reduced individual spending and reduced environmental cost
quests.hint: The two claimed benefits are listed in the last sentence.
quests.explanation: The passage says advocates believe tool libraries reduce both spending and the environmental cost of manufacturing.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct answer.
quests.passage: [A Debate Over Open Office Hours] When a university professor began offering unscheduled 'open office hours' instead of requiring appointments, initial concerns about being overwhelmed by visitors proved largely unfounded. Attendance data collected over the semester showed that students appreciated the flexibility, but most still visited during predictable times, such as the week before major exams.
quests.question: What did the attendance data reveal about student visits?
options: Most students still visited during predictable times like exam weeks
Students visited constantly throughout the semester
Almost no students used the open hours
Visits were spread evenly with no pattern
quests.correctAnswer: Most students still visited during predictable times like exam weeks
quests.hint: The pattern in visits is described in the last sentence.
quests.explanation: The passage says data showed most visits still clustered around predictable times, such as before major exams.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct answer.
quests.passage: [A Look at Noise-Canceling Technology in Cities] City planners in several dense urban areas are experimenting with 'quiet zones' near hospitals and schools, using sound-absorbing pavement and staggered traffic signals to reduce noise without banning vehicles outright. Early measurements suggest these zones can lower average noise levels by several decibels during peak traffic hours.
quests.question: How do the quiet zones reduce noise, according to the passage?
options: Banning all vehicles from the area
Sound-absorbing pavement and staggered traffic signals
Requiring drivers to use electric cars
Closing the streets during the day
quests.correctAnswer: Sound-absorbing pavement and staggered traffic signals
quests.hint: The methods used are listed in the first sentence.
quests.explanation: The passage says the zones use sound-absorbing pavement and staggered traffic signals to reduce noise.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct answer.
quests.passage: [A Shift in How Museums Fund Exhibits] Facing reduced government funding, several museums have turned to corporate sponsorships to finance major exhibits, a shift that has sparked debate among curators. Supporters argue sponsorships allow ambitious exhibits to continue, while critics worry that sponsors may subtly influence which stories a museum chooses to tell.
quests.question: What do critics worry about regarding corporate sponsorships?
options: Sponsorships will end government funding entirely
Museums will need to raise ticket prices
Sponsors will demand exhibits close early
Sponsors may subtly influence which stories are told
quests.correctAnswer: Sponsors may subtly influence which stories are told
quests.hint: The critics' concern is stated in the last sentence.
quests.explanation: The passage says critics worry sponsors may subtly influence which stories a museum chooses to tell.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct answer.
quests.passage: [A Study on Multitasking] A widely cited study found that people who frequently switch between tasks, such as checking messages while working, take significantly longer to complete each task than those who focus on one thing at a time. Researchers attribute this to the mental effort required to refocus attention after every interruption, even brief ones.
quests.question: What do researchers attribute the slower completion times to?
options: A general decline in overall intelligence
The mental effort required to refocus after interruptions
The number of tasks being completed
A lack of proper training
quests.correctAnswer: The mental effort required to refocus after interruptions
quests.hint: The researchers' explanation is given in the last sentence.
quests.explanation: The passage says researchers attribute the slower times to the mental effort needed to refocus after interruptions.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct answer.
quests.passage: [A Company's Approach to Whistleblower Reports] After several high-profile scandals in other industries, one company introduced an anonymous reporting system that allows employees to flag ethical concerns without revealing their identity, even to senior management. Early internal data suggests reports have increased since the system launched, which leadership interprets as a sign of greater trust rather than a growing number of problems.
quests.question: How does leadership interpret the increase in reports?
options: As a sign of greater trust in the system
As proof of a sudden rise in misconduct
As a reason to discontinue the system
As evidence employees are misusing it
quests.correctAnswer: As a sign of greater trust in the system
quests.hint: Leadership's interpretation is explained in the last sentence.
quests.explanation: The passage says leadership interprets the rise in reports as a sign of greater trust, not more problems.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct answer.
quests.passage: [A Look at Vertical Farming] Vertical farms, which grow crops in stacked layers inside climate-controlled buildings, use significantly less land and water than traditional farming, though the high cost of the necessary lighting and climate systems has so far limited the produce to premium price ranges. Some companies are betting that falling equipment costs will eventually make vertical farming competitive with conventional agriculture.
quests.question: What has limited vertical farm produce to premium price ranges?
options: A shortage of available crops to grow
The high cost of lighting and climate systems
Strict government regulations on farming
A lack of consumer interest in the produce
quests.correctAnswer: The high cost of lighting and climate systems
quests.hint: The cause is explained in the middle of the passage.
quests.explanation: The passage says the high cost of lighting and climate systems has kept prices in the premium range.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct answer.
quests.passage: [A Debate Over AI-Generated Art in Competitions] When a piece of AI-assisted artwork won a regional art competition, it reignited a long-running debate about what should count as authorship in creative work. Supporters of the entry argued that selecting prompts and refining results still requires artistic judgment, while critics maintained that the process lacks the manual skill traditionally rewarded in such competitions.
quests.question: What did critics of the AI-assisted entry argue?
options: The artwork was technically impossible to create
The competition should be cancelled entirely
AI art requires no human involvement at all
The process lacks the manual skill traditionally rewarded
quests.correctAnswer: The process lacks the manual skill traditionally rewarded
quests.hint: The critics' position is explained in the last sentence.
quests.explanation: The passage says critics argued the process lacks the manual skill traditionally rewarded in art competitions.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct answer.
quests.passage: [A Rise in Skill-Sharing Networks] Skill-sharing networks connect neighbors willing to trade services, such as tutoring or basic home repairs, without any money changing hands, relying instead on a system of earned credits. Members typically earn credits by offering their own skills, which they can later spend on services they need from someone else in the network.
quests.question: How do members typically earn credits in the network?
options: By offering their own skills to others
By paying a small monthly fee
By recruiting new members
By donating unused household items
quests.correctAnswer: By offering their own skills to others
quests.hint: The method of earning credits is described in the last sentence.
quests.explanation: The passage says members earn credits by offering their own skills to other members of the network.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct answer.
quests.passage: [A Look at Delayed School Start Times] After adolescent sleep researchers presented evidence that teenagers' biological clocks naturally shift later than those of younger children, several school districts delayed their start times by nearly an hour. Attendance records from the first year showed a modest but measurable drop in both tardiness and reported daytime sleepiness among students.
quests.question: What did attendance records show after start times were delayed?
options: A large increase in student absences
No measurable change of any kind
A rise in after-school activity participation
A modest drop in tardiness and daytime sleepiness
quests.correctAnswer: A modest drop in tardiness and daytime sleepiness
quests.hint: The result is described in the last sentence.
quests.explanation: The passage says records showed a modest but measurable drop in tardiness and daytime sleepiness.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct answer.
quests.passage: [A Company's Shift to Employee-Owned Structure] When the founder of a mid-sized manufacturing company retired, rather than selling the business to a larger competitor, she transferred ownership shares to her long-term employees through a structured buyout plan. Employees say the change has noticeably increased their sense of investment in the company's long-term success.
quests.question: What effect have employees reported since the ownership change?
options: A noticeably increased sense of investment in long-term success
A significant decrease in their daily workload
Immediate and substantial pay increases
Less interest in the company's future
quests.correctAnswer: A noticeably increased sense of investment in long-term success
quests.hint: The employees' reported effect is in the last sentence.
quests.explanation: The passage says employees report a noticeably increased sense of investment in the company's long-term success.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct answer.
quests.passage: [A Debate Over Algorithmic Hiring Tools] Some companies now use software to screen job applications before a human ever reviews them, a practice intended to reduce the time spent on manual sorting. Critics point out that these tools can inadvertently filter out qualified candidates whose résumés simply use different keywords than the algorithm was trained to expect.
quests.question: What concern do critics raise about algorithmic hiring tools?
options: They take longer than manual review
They cannot be used for entry-level jobs
They can filter out qualified candidates using different keywords
They require candidates to pay a fee
quests.correctAnswer: They can filter out qualified candidates using different keywords
quests.hint: The critics' concern is explained in the last sentence.
quests.explanation: The passage says critics worry the tools may filter out qualified candidates whose résumés use different keywords.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct answer.
quests.passage: [A Look at Passive House Design] Buildings constructed to 'passive house' standards use thick insulation, airtight construction, and heat-recovery ventilation to maintain a comfortable indoor temperature with drastically less energy than conventional buildings. Owners often report heating costs up to ninety percent lower, though the higher upfront construction cost remains a barrier for many builders.
quests.question: What remains a barrier to passive house construction, according to the passage?
options: A lack of available insulation materials
The higher upfront construction cost
Poor indoor air quality
Government restrictions on the design
quests.correctAnswer: The higher upfront construction cost
quests.hint: The barrier is mentioned at the very end of the passage.
quests.explanation: The passage says the higher upfront construction cost remains a barrier for many builders.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct answer.
quests.passage: [A Study on Bilingual Children] Researchers studying bilingual children found that while these children sometimes reach certain vocabulary milestones slightly later in each individual language, they consistently outperform monolingual peers on tasks requiring mental flexibility, such as switching quickly between different rules in a game. Scientists believe managing two languages provides ongoing practice for this kind of cognitive flexibility.
quests.question: What do bilingual children consistently outperform monolingual peers on?
options: Tasks requiring physical coordination
Tasks measuring vocabulary size alone
Tasks requiring mental flexibility
Tasks involving memorization of facts
quests.correctAnswer: Tasks requiring mental flexibility
quests.hint: The specific skill is named in the second sentence.
quests.explanation: The passage says bilingual children consistently outperform peers on tasks requiring mental flexibility.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct answer.
quests.passage: [A Debate Over Gig Economy Protections] As more workers earn income through app-based gig platforms rather than traditional employment, lawmakers in several regions have debated whether such workers should receive benefits like paid sick leave, which are traditionally tied to formal employment status. Platform companies argue that added benefits could threaten the flexible scheduling that many workers say they value most.
quests.question: What do platform companies argue could happen if benefits are added?
options: It would eliminate gig work entirely
It would lower how much customers pay
It could threaten the flexible scheduling workers value
It would require workers to reapply for jobs
quests.correctAnswer: It could threaten the flexible scheduling workers value
quests.hint: The companies' argument is stated in the last sentence.
quests.explanation: The passage says platform companies argue added benefits could threaten the flexible scheduling many workers value.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct answer.
quests.passage: [A Look at Adaptive Reuse in Architecture] Instead of demolishing an old textile factory, a city redeveloped the building into apartments and shared workspaces, preserving much of its original brick structure and large windows. Architects who specialize in this kind of adaptive reuse argue it is often more sustainable than new construction, since it avoids the environmental cost of producing entirely new building materials.
quests.question: Why do architects argue adaptive reuse is often more sustainable?
options: It avoids the environmental cost of new building materials
It is always cheaper than new construction
It requires no government approval
It uses only recycled furniture
quests.correctAnswer: It avoids the environmental cost of new building materials
quests.hint: The sustainability argument is explained in the last sentence.
quests.explanation: The passage says architects argue reuse avoids the environmental cost of producing new building materials.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct answer.
quests.passage: [A Look at Corporate Four-Day Weeks and Client Expectations] When a consulting firm switched to a four-day work week, one unexpected challenge was managing client expectations, since some clients were accustomed to reaching consultants on the firm's traditional fifth day. The firm resolved this by clearly communicating new response-time policies in advance, which most clients accepted without complaint.
quests.question: How did the firm resolve the challenge with client expectations?
options: By clearly communicating new response-time policies in advance
By returning to a five-day work week
By hiring additional staff to cover the fifth day
By offering clients a discount on services
quests.correctAnswer: By clearly communicating new response-time policies in advance
quests.hint: The firm's solution is described in the last sentence.
quests.explanation: The passage says the firm resolved the issue by communicating new response-time policies in advance.
